correctness.rationale: Two pair-read errors require cyclic pair distance at least five between codewords of different information weight. The exact pair-shadow identity d_pair(x,y)=|T∪(T−1)| for difference support T handles ≥4 changed message bits immediately (n≥5). For three changed message bits, suffix difference 101 or 111 gives two additional fresh suffix edges; for two, different weights force ±2 and suffix 010 supplies two fresh edges; for one, suffix 101 or 111 touches four suffix-adjacent cyclic edges and at least one changed prefix edge is outside that set when k≥2. These cases exhaust all pairs. Any r≤2 suffix fails comparing 0^k with a 1 in last information position: all differences lie in ≤3 consecutive positions and touch ≤4 pair reads; k=1 needs total block length ≥5 and 00000/11111 attains it. An independent cyclic pair-distance enumerator checked all unequal-weight message pairs for k=2..9 (106,762 pairs at k=9), with exact minimum five. The infinite-length guarantee rests on the edge argument.

value.rationale: Exact constant redundancy for a basic information statistic under overlapping-read errors is a natural coding-theory design target; three check bits are proven both necessary and sufficient for every k≥2, with an explicit four-periodic systematic encoder. It is a sharp structural guarantee distinct from full-message recovery, not an isolated numerical bound.

final_claim: For systematic binary encoding to protect the ordinary information Hamming-weight function against at most two cyclic symbol-pair read errors, the minimum redundancy is r=4 for k=1 and r=3 for every k≥2; for k≥2 append (w mod2,⌊w/2⌋ mod2,w mod2), where w is information weight.
